name: French Lick Springs Hotel
scope: Standing French Lick Springs Hotel, with the Main, West, Deluxe and North wings, the southeast Annex, connecting ranges, east veranda and Spa Wing.
era: Contemporary hotel after the 2006 reopening and restoration of the early twentieth-century wings.

references.caption: Front and southern end of the French Lick Springs Hotel, located at 8670 W. State Road 56 in French Lick, Indiana, United States.  Built in 1902 and since converted into a casino, it and the surrounding grounds are listed together on the National Register of Historic Places.
references.alt: Front and southern end of the French Lick Springs Hotel, located at 8670 W. State Road 56 in French Lick, Indiana, United States.  Built in 1902 and since converted into a casino, it and the surrounding grounds are listed together on the National Register of Historic Places.
categories: National Register of Historic Places with known IDs

originalReview.notes: The standing hotel seen from the southeast. It clearly resolves the two-storey former baths, buff brick, tall annex tower, lighter cornices, round-headed upper sashes and east veranda.

review.method: Exact Qualla photographer dedication with the hotel’s mapped footprint and National Register written survey
review.notes: The exact public-domain Nyttend original confirms the current southeast hotel facade. The 1880s image depicts a predecessor. Governors and garden imagery and the independent Pluto Spring pavilion do not document the selected hotel exterior. The National Register description provides relative footprint and height controls and the resort identifies current wing use.
